guides.control_name: Remote Desktop Services Remote Code Execution
guides.vulnerability_name: Remote Desktop Services Remote Code Execution
guides.recommended_action:
Recommended monitoring actions:
- Continuously monitor RDP-related logs and authentication events for hosts affected by CVE-2019-0708.
- Configure alerts for unusual remote desktop access attempts, repeated failures, and suspicious session patterns.
- Review exposed RDP services regularly to verify patch effectiveness and confirm reduced attack exposure.
- Correlate endpoint, firewall, and Windows event logs to detect exploitation attempts or abnormal lateral movement.
- Escalate confirmed suspicious activity for incident review and document follow-up actions for auditor traceability.

implementation_steps.title: Verify Patch Installation for CVE-2019-0708
implementation_steps.description: Check if the system has installed the security update addressing CVE-2019-0708.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Output displays KB4490077 or later in the HotFixID column.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the output of the Get-HotFix command as proof of patch installation.

implementation_steps.title: Check RDP Service Status
implementation_steps.description: Verify if the Remote Desktop Services (TermService) is running.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Output shows 'Status' as 'Running' for the TermService.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture the service status output to confirm RDP is active.

implementation_steps.title: Monitor RDP-Related Security Events
implementation_steps.description: Collect Security Event Logs for RDP logon attempts and authentication failures.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Output lists events with IDs 4622 (successful logon), 4624 (interactive logon), or 4672 (special privilege assigned) containing 'RDP' in the message.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Export the filtered event logs to a CSV file for analysis.

implementation_steps.title: Configure Audit Policies for RDP Access
implementation_steps.description: Enable auditing for remote interactive logon events to detect suspicious RDP activity.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Command output confirms success: 'The audit policy was successfully modified.'
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture the command output to verify audit policy changes.

implementation_steps.title: Validate Firewall RDP Rule Configuration
implementation_steps.description: Check if the Windows Firewall allows RDP traffic (port 3389) and verify rule details.
commands: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all | findstr /i "RDP"
implementation_steps.expected_result: Output displays rules allowing TCP port 3389 with 'Remote Desktop' in the name.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the firewall rule output to confirm exposure status.

implementation_steps.title: Correlate Logs with SIEM for Anomalies
implementation_steps.description: Manually configure SIEM (e.g., Splunk, ELK) to correlate RDP events with authentication failures and lateral movement patterns.
implementation_steps.expected_result: SIEM dashboard displays alerts for repeated RDP failures, non-standard hours, or unusual user behavior.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture a screenshot of the SIEM correlation rules and alert triggers.

implementation_steps.title: Verify Vulnerability Exposure via Scan
implementation_steps.description: Run a vulnerability scanner to confirm CVE-2019-0708 exposure post-patching.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Scan report indicates 'No vulnerability detected' for CVE-2019-0708.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the OpenVAS scan report as evidence of patch effectiveness.

guides.recommended_action:

- Monitor **Failed Login Attempts** with real-time alerting for thresholds exceeding 9 per hour, log all failed attempts, and escalate to security for investigation using ISO 27002 8.16 (Monitoring activities).  
- Monitor **Access Frequency** for anomalies exceeding 18 accesses per hour, implement automated anomaly detection, and schedule daily reviews of access logs per ISO 27002 8.16 (Monitoring activities).

- Monitor **Password Resets** for activity exceeding 4 resets per week, log all reset events with justification, and require supervisor approval for resets above this threshold per ISO 27002 5.17 (Authentication information).  
- Monitor **Session Duration** for sessions exceeding 11.1 hours, trigger alerts for prolonged sessions, and enforce automatic session termination after 12 hours to mitigate unauthorized access risks using ISO 27002 8.16 (Monitoring activities).
